title: Chapter 42: Sixty Seconds
html:
The bathroom fell away from his senses. Darkness pressed in on every side, and the only thing he could hear clearly was his own heartbeat.

Nothing moved in the corridor. Even the mirror entity seemed absent.

The appointed moment arrived. Chen Ge focused on the names of his parents as the phone instructed, refusing to let the strange sensation break his concentration.

The candlelight stretched into a thin, distant glow. In an instant, the impossible feeling of deep water closed around him completely.

The ritual had begun.

Cold seemed to surround him from every direction. He knew he was still in the bathroom, yet his senses insisted that he was descending into a lightless depth.

Sound vanished until only the dull pounding of his heart remained. The darkness felt immense, as though the little bathroom had opened onto an endless abyss.

Chen Ge emptied his mind of everything except his parents’ names and waited.

Stay calm. Let the mission run its course.

The experience was unlike anything he had encountered before. The wavering candlelight seemed impossibly far away, like a star seen from the bottom of an ocean.

Mom. Dad.

Time lost all meaning. Chen Ge repeated their names silently, concentrating on the memory of their faces while the darkness pulled at his awareness.

Pressure built around him. Whether it was part of the illusion or something else, his body reacted as though the abyss were becoming real.

How much longer?

His heartbeat sounded louder. The sensation around his throat and chest tightened, and unease began to overwhelm concentration.

Chen Ge opened his eyes, but the darkness did not change. For several seconds, he had the disorienting impression that he had crossed into an entirely different place.

It should be almost over… right?

Then a violent ripple passed through the darkness, followed by a sound from beyond the bathroom. It was impossibly clear, as if something wanted him to notice it.

Footsteps? In the corridor?

His pulse jumped, and every muscle in his body tensed.That has to be the mirror entity. I just need the dolls to keep it away until the phone ends the ritual.

A low buzzing filled his ears. He clung to the memory of his parents and tried not to let the footsteps pull his attention away.

Don’t lose focus.

The footsteps quickened. Whether the strange acoustics were distorting them or not, they sounded as though whoever was outside had begun to hurry toward the bathroom.

The pressure intensified until the illusion became physically convincing. Chen Ge’s thoughts slowed, but stubbornness kept him from breaking the ritual early.

BANG! BANG! BANG!

Something struck the bathroom door. The sudden impact shattered what remained of Chen Ge’s composure.

After several more blows, the noise stopped. Perhaps the doll by the door had interfered again. Silence returned, but Chen Ge no longer believed the ritual was harmless.

He had reached the point where instinct told him to stop. Whatever the black phone was showing him, his body was reacting as though the danger were real.

Enough.

His thoughts blurred. Childhood memories rose without warning—his parents beside him, the Haunted House before everything changed, fragments of ordinary days he had not realized he treasured.

Only then did he understand the mission description. The “boundary” was not a poetic metaphor. The ritual was forcing his senses toward some threshold he did not understand.

“It is said to bring the boundary between the living and the dead close enough for you to glimpse someone who has passed beyond it.”

Whatever the mechanism, the experience made that boundary feel terrifyingly real.

Chen Ge stared into the darkness, searching for a familiar face. None appeared. There was only silence and the oppressive sense of something waiting beyond sight.

The pressure became unbearable.

No. I’m ending this now.

His parents had not appeared. Even through the fear, relief rose in him: perhaps that meant they were still alive.

Chen Ge broke concentration and tried to pull away from the ritual. For an instant, the pressure eased—then something changed.

An unseen force caught him and dragged his awareness back toward the darkness.

The dolls were guarding the room, and the mirror entity should not have been able to approach unnoticed. So what was holding him there?

Panic surged through him. Chen Ge fought the pull with everything he had, reaching blindly for something solid in the real bathroom.

The strain had pushed both his body and concentration to their limits.

His hand struck the edge of the tub with a sharp crack. At the same instant, the pressure vanished.

Chen Ge jerked upright, dragging in air as the bathroom snapped back into focus.
